title: Give the PIM Manager a custom host name
purpose: Gives the PIM Manager a custom host name (for example pim-manager.<your domain>) next to its generated Container Apps address: it adds and binds the name with a certificate, writes or prints the DNS records, and adds the name to the Manager's known host names and its sign-in reply URLs.
whenToRun: After the installation, when people should reach the Manager on a name in your own domain. A public environment takes a public subdomain you own and a free managed certificate (create the printed CNAME and TXT records first, then re-run with -PublicDnsReady -- also with -Dns None); a private environment needs your own certificate (Key Vault PFX or PEM, or a PFX file) and a private DNS record: written into a private DNS zone that already exists, or printed for your DNS administrator (AD DNS). Run it again with -Remove to take the name off. It is part of the PIM Manager release package, not a separate download: run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia (or the guided install) downloaded and verified (.\tools\setup\Set-PimManagerCustomHost.ps1).

runAs.name: Contributor
runAs.why: Adds (or with -Remove removes) the host name and the certificate on the Manager container app and its environment, and sets PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES (a new revision).

runAs.name: Private DNS Zone Contributor
runAs.scope: -PrivateDnsResourceGroup (default: the PIM resource group); only for a private environment with -Dns Auto / PrivateDnsZone
runAs.why: Lists the private DNS zones there, writes the A record into the EXISTING zone the name belongs to and links it to the -LinkVnetIds networks that are not linked yet. PIM never creates a zone.

runAs.name: Network Contributor
runAs.scope: each virtual network in -LinkVnetIds (only when a link is created)
runAs.why: Linking a private DNS zone to a virtual network needs join rights on that network.

runAs.name: Key Vault Secrets User
runAs.scope: the Key Vault named by -KeyVaultName (only with a Key Vault certificate)
runAs.why: Reads the certificate (its secret half: a PFX, or PEM that is converted to PFX in memory) straight into the upload; it is never written to disk.

runAs.name: Application Administrator (or owner of the Manager's sign-in app registration)
runAs.scope: the Manager's Easy Auth app registration (skipped with -SkipEasyAuth)
runAs.why: Adds (or with -Remove removes) https://<name>/.auth/login/aad/callback in its reply URLs.

changes.object: custom domain <name> (hostname add), then bound to its certificate (SNI); -Remove takes it off
changes.scope: the Manager app only; the other names and the app's secrets are kept
changes.why: The point of the script: the Manager answers on the new name.
changes.undo: Run the script again with -Remove (or remove the custom domain in the Azure portal > Container App > Custom domains).

changes.object: a managed certificate (public environment) or an uploaded certificate from Key Vault (PFX or PEM) / PFX file (private environment), named after the host name
changes.why: The name needs a certificate; a private environment cannot validate a free managed one.
changes.undo: -Remove deletes it when nothing else uses it (or delete it from the environment after removing the custom domain).

changes.object: the A record <name> -> the environment's static IP in the EXISTING zone the name belongs to (the longest private zone the name ends with, or -DnsZone), and a link to each -LinkVnetIds network not linked to that zone yet. No zone is created: when none exists, the zone, record and links to create are printed
changes.why: So clients in those networks resolve the name. The record is read before it is written.
changes.undo: Delete the A record (and the links if nothing else uses them). -Remove prints the record to delete; it deletes no DNS.

changes.object: PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES (the name appended once; -Remove takes it out) -- a new revision
changes.why: The Manager knows the custom name. Mail links (the ManagerUrl setting) switch to it on the next signed-in Manager page only when ManagerUrl is empty or was auto-recorded as the generated address; a ManagerUrl set in Settings is never overwritten.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (or remove the name from PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES).

changes.object: the Manager's sign-in app registration: reply URL https://<name>/.auth/login/aad/callback
changes.why: Sign-in on the new name returns to the Manager.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (or remove the reply URL from the app registration).

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id. The REST session is pinned to it; a session of any other tenant is refused.

parameters.name: HostName
parameters.help: The custom name, at least three labels (name.domain.tld). A public environment refuses private top-level names (.local, .corp, .lan, ...).

parameters.name: KeyVaultName
parameters.help: The Key Vault holding your certificate (with -KeyVaultCertName).

parameters.name: KeyVaultCertName
parameters.help: The certificate's name in that Key Vault. PFX (PKCS #12) or PEM content type; PEM is converted to PFX in memory and needs PowerShell 7.

parameters.name: PfxPath
parameters.help: Your certificate as a PFX file, instead of Key Vault.

parameters.name: Dns
parameters.help: Auto (private environment: private DNS zone; public: print the public records), PrivateDnsZone, AdDns (print the record for your DNS administrator; PIM writes no AD DNS) or None (no DNS step; a public environment still needs -PublicDnsReady).

parameters.name: PrivateDnsResourceGroup
parameters.help: Where your existing private DNS zone lives (for example the hub's DNS resource group). The longest zone there that the name ends with is used.

parameters.name: LinkVnetIds
parameters.help: Resource ids of the virtual networks whose clients must resolve the name. Each is linked to the zone unless it is already linked (under any link name).

parameters.name: DnsZone
parameters.default: AdDns: the name minus its first label; PrivateDnsZone: the longest existing zone
parameters.help: The DNS zone the name lives in, when the default is wrong (e.g. pim-manager.corp.contoso.local in zone contoso.local).

parameters.name: AdDnsServer
parameters.help: -Dns AdDns: only fills the DNS server name into the printed lines. PIM never connects to it.

parameters.name: PublicDnsReady
parameters.help: Public environment (-Dns Auto or None): the CNAME and TXT records exist, so the name can be validated and bound. Without it the script stops after printing them.

parameters.name: SkipEasyAuth
parameters.help: Do not add (or remove) the reply URL in the sign-in app registration.

parameters.name: Remove
parameters.help: Take the name off: remove the binding and the certificate the script uploaded for it, the name from PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES and the reply URL. Prints the DNS record to delete; PIM deletes no DNS and never a zone.

readsOnly: the Manager container app and its Container Apps environment (internal or external, static IP, default domain, verification id)
the private DNS zones in -PrivateDnsResourceGroup, the existing record and the zone's virtual network links (before writing them)
the Manager's Easy Auth configuration and its app registration's reply URLs
whatIf: Reads the Manager app and its environment (and the private DNS zones), prints the plan (certificate type, DNS mode and every DNS record), then 'What if: Performing the operation "custom host name <name>" on target "ca-pim-manager"' and 'preview only -- nothing was changed'. Nothing is written. With -Remove the removal is previewed the same way.
undo: Run the script again with -Remove: it removes the custom domain from the Manager app, deletes its certificate from the environment (when unused), removes the name from PIM_MANAGER_HOSTNAMES and the reply URL from the sign-in app registration, and prints the DNS record for you to delete.
